title: Signature Claim parsing — Patent Document Extractor
description: Signature original — Claims are numbered sentences defining legal scope; parsers split and number them. Claims are the patent's heart. Scope is everything. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# Patent extraction: parse claims (independent vs dependent), classifications, inventors.
text = """Claims\n1. A widget comprising A and B.\n2. The widget of claim 1, further comprising C.\nInventors\nAmy Lee\nClassifications\nG06F 17/30""".replace("\\n", "\n")
import re
claims, inventors, classes = [], [], []
sec = None
for line in text.splitlines():
    s = line.strip()
    if s.lower().startswith("claims"): sec = "claims"; continue
    if s.lower().startswith("inventors"): sec = "inv"; continue
    if s.lower().startswith("classifications"): sec = "cls"; continue
    m = re.match(r"^(\d+)\.\s*(.*)", s)
    if sec == "claims" and m:
        n, body = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
        dep = re.search(r"claim (\d+)", body, re.I)
        claims.append({"n": n, "independent": not dep, "depends_on": int(dep.group(1)) if dep else None, "text": body[:50]})
    elif sec == "inv" and s: inventors.append(s)
    elif sec == "cls" and s: classes.append(s)
print(f"claims: {len(claims)} ({sum(1 for c in claims if c['independent'])} independent)")
for c in claims:
    print(f"  claim {c['n']}: independent={c['independent']} depends_on={c['depends_on']} :: {c['text']}")
print("inventors:", inventors)
print("classifications:", classes)
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.
